cases.name: Selena F. Miller Mowen
cases.about:
She was a registered nurse for about 12 years, and she worked for the last six years as a nurse advocate for a Franklin County’s women’s shelter for victims of domestic violence. “She was the love of my life. She was God’s gift,” Sharon Miller said. She described her daughter as deeply caring of others, as well as animals, but who also loved to joke and tease. Whether it was rescuing dogs or bottle-feeding a baby rabbit back to health before releasing it back into the wild, Jack Miller said his daughter’s love for animals was unparalleled. Selena served in the military before getting a medical discharge, then spent 13 or 14 years as a nurse all over the country before joining Women in Need. Life-long friend Jodi Garlock McQuade said that job meant everything to Selena, even if it meant she had to take a pay cut. McQuade said Selena tried to get her to join the organization, telling her things like “You would love it and you’d be good. Just forget the money, and do it. You will love what you do.”

https://www.pennlive.com/news/2021/12/nurse-who-worked-at-domestic-violence-shelter-killed-in-murder-suicide-i-wish-she-could-have-helped-herself.html?fbclid=IwAR2Q5KoAIF43OGGQZfo2_H13ezJLBAZgc_v-M4z7z0qRHCll9qA7wxN4fF4

Her obituary said, "Selena went on to obtain her nursing degree from Viriginia Commonwealth University. She was employed as a forensic nurse for Women in Need. Selena also served in the United States Army. She was a member of the Charles Nitterhouse VFW Post 1599, Chambersburg. Selena loved the beach and sky-diving. She was a fan of racing and especially a fan of Chase Elliott as well as a Pittsburgh Steelers and Pirates fan and a Baltimore Orioles fan."
